key_insight: Density functional simulations predict that certain shear strains transform monolayer h-BN into an ordered orthorhombic pmmm phase with a narrow band gap of approximately 0.65 eV.
engineering_relevance: Strain-induced phase transformation could offer a route to semiconducting 2D boron nitride for electronic applications.
method: First-principles density functional theory using pseudopotentials and PBE exchange-correlation.
Structural simulations under different strain types and directions.
Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics and electronic-structure analysis.
evidence_signal: The simulations indicate thermal stability of the predicted orthorhombic phase up to approximately 900 K and a band gap of approximately 0.65 eV.
watch_item: The phase remains a theoretical prediction; experimental accessibility under strong shear and the accuracy of the PBE band gap require validation.
paper_title: Strain-induced structural transformations in hexagonal monolayer boron nitride. A density functional study
